topic: Great Red Spot is wider than Earth
claim: Jupiter's Great Red Spot is a swirling oval of clouds about twice as wide as Earth, observed for more than 300 years, and Juno found it reaches about 300 miles below the cloud tops.

beats.caption: Twice as wide as Earth
beats.vo: This storm is twice as wide as Earth.

beats.caption: Jupiter's Great Red Spot
beats.vo: It's Jupiter's Great Red Spot, a swirling oval of clouds. Astronomers have watched it for more than 300 years.

beats.caption: Jupiter is 11x wider
beats.vo: Jupiter itself is 11 times wider than Earth, so there's plenty of room for a storm this big.

beats.caption: About 300 miles deep
beats.vo: NASA's Juno spacecraft found it's deep, too. The storm reaches about 300 miles below the cloud tops, in an atmosphere of hydrogen and helium.

beats.caption: Centuries, not days
beats.vo: A hurricane on Earth fades in days or weeks. This one has lasted centuries. What keeps it going?

sources.text: NASA Science, Jupiter Facts: Great Red Spot is a swirling oval of clouds twice as wide as Earth, observed for more than 300 years; Juno gravity data constrain its extent to about 300 miles (500 km) below the cloud tops; atmosphere of hydrogen and helium. https://science.nasa.gov/jupiter/jupiter-facts/ Also: Jupiter is 11 times wider than Earth.
